m.t: Making extra fine sand with Telekinetic Grind
m.pg: Money making guide/Making extra fine sand with Telekinetic Grind

rq.h: or Small rune pouch or Large rune pouch

m.h:
The experience and profit assumes the usage of the listed optional items. If one or more of these items aren't used, the profit and experience may be lower than expected.

As the amount of sandstone ground in an hour exceeds the buy limit of 10,000 an hour, sandstone needs to be either bought from other players, or bought ahead of time, before using this money making method. Grinding one specific type of sandstone might earn the player more gp/hr than grinding all types of sandstone equally. Though, due to the buy limit of 10,000, all sandstone types are listed to allow this method to work more consistently.

Approximately 2,000 inventories can be processed in an hour, assuming an average of 3 ticks (1.8s) to process an inventory. It is theoretically possible to process up to 6,000 inventories per hour, though this would require robot-like click precision and no mistakes or lag.

The following setup involves the least amount of clicking for processing large amounts of Extra Fine Sand in 3 ticks.

  • Stand at a one-click bank (such as the one in War's retreat).
  • Zoom in so that the clickable area of the bank is as large as possible.
  • Place the inventory on your screen so that it is right next to the bank. This way, the mouse only needs to move by a tiny bit to navigate between the bank and the inventory window.
  • Place Telekinetic Grind on an action bar slot for which the key bind is easily accessible.
  • Create a preset containing 28 of the same type of sandstone to grind. Make sure this preset uses the same key bind as the previous step

Now, use the following steps to grind the sandstone.

  • Click to open the bank (tick 1)
  • Press key bind to load the preset (tick 2)
  • As soon as the bank closes, press the key bind button again and select the sandstone in the inventory (tick 3)

With a bit of practice, a player can get very consistent at grinding an inventory of sand in only 3 game ticks.

A similar setup for faster processing looks like:

  • Press key bind and click a sandstone to process it
  • On the same tick, right-click the bank to load your last preset
  • Repeat

This method doesn't require a bank screen to appear or disappear, theoretically saving 2 ticks, though it requires much more precision to click on smaller targets without mistake.

m.pg: Money making guide/Making ghostly ink
Money making guide/Making ghostly ink
Money making guide/Making ghostly ink
m.post: To create ghostly ink, the player should create a preset with 260 of the corresponding necroplasm, 13 vials of water, and 13 ashes. Then load the preset, either click the necroplasm in inventory or add it to an action bar and press the key for it to open the crafting interface, craft the ink, and repeat. It takes 1.2 seconds (2 ticks) to craft ink, so a full inventory takes 15.6 seconds. If the player spends 2.4 seconds (4 ticks) per inventory banking, this allows up to 2,600 ink to be made per hour, although Necroplasm has a buy limit of 50,000 every four hours.

m.pg: Money making guide/Making guam potions
m.h:
Guam potion (unfinished) are used to create attack potions. Players can avoid the tedium of making unfinished potions and buy them directly from the Grand Exchange. This opens up an opportunity to make unfinished guam potions for profit. Before buying the ingredients in bulk, make sure that the method is profitable by making one unfinished potion and testing the profit.

Creating a preset loadout with 14 clean guam and 14 vials of water. Using preset loadouts will help speed up the number of unfinished potions per hour by reducing the intermediary steps; depositing your unfinished potions and withdrawing 14 herbs and vials. Each inventory should take about 21 seconds with banking, which means you can make around 2,400 potions per hour.

To find the current location of a Portable well, ask in the "portables" Friends chat.

m.t: Making harralander tar with Telekinetic Grind
m.pg: Money making guide/Making harralander tar with Telekinetic Grind
m.h:
Make a bank preset with 2 astral runes, 1 law rune, 375 swamp tar, and 25 clean harralander. You can use the law staff and/or the large rune pouch to save inventory spaces and increase profits. Load the preset and then cast the spell Telekinetic Grind. This will instantly generate 375 harralander tar.

This method assumes you average 5 seconds per inventory, or 720.0 inventories completed per hour. Use the input at the top of the page to adjust this number based on your speed.

You will not be able to buy enough swamp tar off the Grand Exchange alone as you can only buy 20,000 swamp tar per 4 hours, whereas this method uses 270,000 swamp tar per hour. You will need to buy from another player in bulk or put in a GE offer for a days/weeks.

m.h:

The urns can be made by going to the Crafting guild and making them at the Potter's wheel. After that, go to the Potter's oven and turn them into Infernal urn (no rune). They can then be deposited in the nearby bank deposit box (or bank chest if hard Falador achievements have been completed). You can combine mining clay and making soft clay to earn more profit.

Portable crafters are recommended for their 10% chance of saving clay and 10% chance of saving unfired urns. This leads to a profit of 7052892-1310910 gp when not buying crafters and 7052892-(1310910 + 28440) gp when buying crafters.

m.pg: Money making guide/Making large historic component crates

rq.h: 5 Archaeology (70 Archaeology (recommended))
Augmented mattock

rq.nt: , rank 5 for 10% (11%) increased artefacts per hour
, rank 5 for 5% (5.5%) of artefacts automatically restored for no materials

rq.h: Flow State relic power recommended for 20% precision (more artefacts per hour)

rq.nt: for faster screening and less hassle

rq.h: or Grace of the elves or Sign of the porter VII

inp.nt: Created using 120 [[incandescent energy]] and 1 [[dragonstone necklace]], other [[Sign of the porter#Types of signs|alternatives]] are available

out.nt: Classic components can be turned into [[Small crate (classic components)|small]] and [[Large crate (classic components)|large crates]] much like the historical components
Timeworn components can be turned into [[Small crate (timeworn components)|small]] and [[Large crate (timeworn components)|large crates]] much like the historical components
Vintage components can be turned into [[Small crate (vintage components)|small]] and [[Large crate (vintage components)|large crates]] much like the historical components

m.h:
The profit rate assumes around 2.4 Third Age iron and Zarosian insignia combined are received per artefact, reducing the amount you need to buy.

You can use Calculator:Archaeology/Hotspot to figure out how many artefacts per hour you can dig up. Disable "Hide low level excavations?" so you can see the venator remains hotspot and enable "Stats for Nerds" to see the artefacts rate. Multiply by 50 or 60 to give yourself 10 minutes to restore artefacts, disassemble items and create the crates.

In this method you create signs of the porter in an amount sufficient for upkeep of an hour, gathering of artefacts from venator remains in the Kharid-et Dig Site (starting from level 5). Then repair the artefacts and disassemble them, followed by disassembling items for protective components and padded parts, to create a large crate (historic components).

Gathering

This method uses Excavating Venator remains as a basis, however instead of selling the materials, you will be repairing the artefacts venator dagger and venator light crossbow to get historical, classic, timeworn, and vintage components from their disassembly.

The auto-screener v1.080 will automatically turn all potential ancient gravel into Third Age iron and Zarosian insignia with a 50/50 chance. This will often increase your monetary yield compared to sifting the ancient gravel, as it can also award many other items - see Money making guide/Screening ancient gravel for comparison.

Gathering is recommended in 65 minute intervals to minimise wasting waterfiend time.

At level 99, players may be able to get 119 artefacts in 65 minutes with least effort (but holding space bar) this equates to about 91 artefacts in 50 minutes as outlined. Check excavation speed to see how much you are expected to make as this method is streamlined for level 70 and 62 artefacts in the 50 minute interval.

Processing

This method requires the disassembly of about 200 items which takes approximately 3 minutes. The prices of protective components and padded parts displayed above are a rough estimation, you should use these calculators to find better options to obtain these materials: protective, padded.

The restoration and disassembly of another 63 artefacts which takes another 7 minutes. The creation of a large crate of historical components requires fewer materials so it is probably more worth-while. After multiple hours, multiple crates of different materials will need to be made to be able to profit from those components, especially classic components.

The average value of disassembling a venator dagger or light crossbow is round 0 gp while the cost of creation is -95,704 gp promising a profit of roughly -95704 round 0 gp per repaired and disassembled piece.

m.pg: Money making guide/Making pastry dough

rq.h: The "Destroy empty containers when cooking" gameplay option needs to be enabled from the Miscellaneous Settings section of the Gameplay Settings.

m.h:
Pastry dough is made by using a pot of flour on a water source. The closest water sources to a bank in free-to-play are the water trough next to the furnace east of the Lumbridge Market, the sink north of Falador's west bank, and the well in Edgeville. Pots of flour can at times be difficult to buy at a low price, but leaving in an offer will usually be successful.

To make this method as efficient as possible, the "Destroy empty containers when cooking" gameplay option should be enabled. This can be done in the Inventory in General Settings section of the Gameplay Settings. This will allow the player to turn 27 pots of flour into dough per trip instead of the usual half-inventory of 14, at the cost of the pots being destroyed.

Withdraw 27 pots of flour from the bank and use one of the pots on the water source. Select pastry dough, and wait about 30 seconds for all of the flour to be converted. Return to the bank, use a bank preset to store the pastry dough and withraw another 27 pots of flour, and repeat. With this method about 80 trips can be done per hour, for 2,160 dough per hour. Sell the pastry dough on the Grand Exchange for as high a price as you can -- the guide price is not always an accurate indicator of what pastry dough is currently selling for.

This is primarily a free-to-play method, but members can also take part, preferably using the sink and Culinaromancer's Chest in the basement of Lumbridge Castle.

m.t: Making pizza bases at Mess Sergeant Ramsey's Cooking Supplies Shop
m.pg: Money making guide/Making pizza bases in Mess Sergeant Ramsey's shop

rq.h: The "Destroy empty containers when cooking" gameplay option needs to be enabled from the Miscellaneous Settings section of the Gameplay Settings.

m.h:
Mess Sergeant Ramsey's Cooking Supplies Shop has a stock of 500 pots of flour that sells for 14 coins each. The stock replenishes at a rate of one per minute and is fully replenished in 8 hours and 20 minutes after being emptied. There is a sink directly behind Ramsey that can be used to turn pots of flour into pizza bases that can be sold for 733 coins each or used as an ingredient in making uncooked pizzas. There is a bank a short distance south of the shop where the pizza bases can be stored.

To get to the shop, use the Taverley lodestone, which takes you right next to the building. Go inside and buy 27 pots of flour (one free inventory space is required so that the empty pots have somewhere to go before they're destroyed), use the sink behind Ramsey to make them into pizza bases, and then run south to the bank to deposit the pizza bases. Since the shop doesn't have a "buy-x" option, getting the right amount of pots of flour requires the player to first select the pot of flour by clicking on it, selecting the Max option from the transaction interface, clicking -1, and then completing the transaction by clicking the Buy button. This makes the process more labour-intensive than it might seem at a first glance, but it's possible to get through the shop's stock in just 25 minutes.

m.pg: Money making guide/Making portents of restoration X
m.h:
Portents of restoration X are portents which restore the life points of the player carrying them when they fall below 50%. As a way to restore life points in an emergency with no input required and no loss of adrenaline, they are quite attractive to players engaging in risky combat encounters. This means creating them can be rather profitable, for those who have the Divination level to do so.

Each portent of restoration X is made from a rocktail and 60 incandescent energy, and can be made anywhere. Up to 27 portents can be made per inventory, from 27 rocktails and 1620 energy. Using bank presets to speed up the banking process is recommended. Even higher rates can be achieved by two-ticking the creation of the portents.

m.pg: Money making guide/Making potion flasks

rq.nt: or better on the tool belt

m.h:
Potion flasks are popular because they can hold 2 more doses per inventory space over vials. Once daily, you can mine up to 75 red sandstone (or 50 if you have not completed the Elite Desert Tasks) which can be turned into potion flasks.

The first location for red sandstone is just outside of Oo'glog. This location can be mined for 50 sand stone a day and is right near the Robust glass machine. Mine a full inventory and then crawl through the adjacent hole into Oo'glog. Run west to the robust glass machine and left click it to convert all your red sandstone to robust glass. After that, blow the glass into flasks and then bank them. Return to the rock outside of Oo'glog and mine the rest of your daily red sandstone, turning those into flasks as well.

Alternatively after Plague's End, the sandstone can be banked using signs of the porter and later turned into glass using the machine in Prifddinas, which is closer to a bank.

If you have completed the Elite Desert Tasks, there is another sandstone rock east of Sophanem that can be mined for extra 25 red sandstone a day. The fastest way to get here is with a Pharaoh's sceptre or a Sceptre of the Gods. A Sophanem Slayer Dungeon teleport tablet is almost as fast. Using the Menaphos lodestone is also an option.

Red sandstone can only be mined once per day, resetting at 00:00 UTC.

With the Shooting Star D&D bonus, it will yield 25% more red sandstones, which will mine on average 93 per day. Combined with Resourceful aura, one can yield 104 on average.

m.pg: Money making guide/Making pyre logs
m.h:
Teak pyre logs are made by combining 3 doses of sacred oil with teak logs. Each pyre log takes 1.2 seconds to make, setting a theoretical maximum of 3000 pyre logs per hour. However, accounting for time spent banking as well as human error and loss of attention, a more realistic figure would likely be roughly 2304 logs, or 144 inventories per hour - higher rates are possible, but hard to maintain.

You can process up to 16 logs per inventory by withdrawing 16 logs and 12 4-dose vials. Use a bank preset to speed this up. The logs are then made into pyre logs by clicking on the sacred oil vials.

Sacred oil has a buy limit of 1000 vials per 4 hours. To help get around this, you may want to buy 3-dose, 2-dose and 1-dose vials and decant them. It is also possible to work around the limit by letting the order fill while doing other activities, directly trading with other players, or by using alternate accounts.

m.pg: Money making guide/Making pyre logs
m.h:
Arctic pyre logs are made by combining 3 doses of sacred oil with arctic pine logs. Each pyre log takes 1.2 seconds to make, setting a theoretical maximum of 3000 pyre logs per hour. However, accounting for time spent banking as well as human error and loss of attention, a more realistic figure would likely be roughly 2304 logs, or 144 inventories per hour - higher rates are possible, but hard to maintain.

You can process up to 16 logs per inventory by withdrawing 16 logs and 12 4-dose vials. Use a bank preset to speed this up. The logs are then made into pyre logs by clicking on the sacred oil vials.

Sacred oil has a buy limit of 1000 vials per 4 hours. To help get around this, you may want to buy 3-dose, 2-dose and 1-dose vials and decant them.

m.pg: Money making guide/Making pyre logs
m.h: Up to 2,500 magic pyre logs can be made per hour by combining four doses of sacred oil with magic logs. While 2,500 is the upper limit on the number of logs that can be made, 2,400 is a more realistic assumption. A major advantage of this method is that it may be performed at the Grand Exchange, allowing players to make even more money by merchanting at the same time. However, a disadvantage of this method is that only 1,000 bottles of sacred oil may be bought on the Grand Exchange every 4 hours. A further complication is that the 4-dose sacred oil is high in demand and low in supply, which makes the 3-dose oil much easier to obtain. Using 3-dose sacred oils decreases the amount of logs per inventory to 12, which in turn decreases profit-per-hour slightly. However, Buying 3-dose oils and having Bob Barter decant them into 4 doses is possible. Using this method also increases the buying limit to 1,750 4-dose oils per hour due to the extra 3,000 doses from 3-dose oils. Note that if you make the sacred oils yourself will increase your profit by several million as it only costs about 100k to make the necessary oils. This method will take several hours if on the official world.
